```{r setup}
res_dir <- "results"
need <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path(res_dir, f)
  if (!file.exists(p)) {
    stop("Missing ", p, ". Run: Rscript run_experiment.R --checks --calibrate",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  utils::read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
checks <- need("checks.csv")
summary <- need("summary.csv")
truths <- need("truths.csv")
meta <- need("metadata.csv")
```

## Question

The Dawid-Skene FIML prototype (study 29, `R/ds_fiml.R`) estimates the
latent-class conditional-independence model by EM and maps the fitted
parameters to model-implied fixed-rater Conger and Fleiss kappas. It now
carries delta-method inference: analytic observed-data scores in softmax
coordinates, observed information by finite differences of the analytic
score, a rank-truncated pseudo-inverse over the softmax gauge, and both an
ML (`vcov_ml`) and a robust sandwich (`vcov_robust`) covariance. Are these
standard errors correct, and how do the two flavours calibrate at the
sample sizes study 29 cares about?

## Short answer

```{r answer, results = "asis"}
ok <- summary[summary$dgp == "ds5x6_severity", ]
band <- range(ok$ratio_robust[ok$n >= 100])
cov_band <- range(ok$cover_robust[ok$n >= 100])
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "All mechanical checks pass (analytic score, observed information, ",
  "gauge rank, bootstrap agreement). On the correctly specified DGP at ",
  "n >= 100, robust-sandwich se/sd ratios span %.2f-%.2f and Wald-z ",
  "coverage spans %.2f-%.2f across mechanisms, weights, and coefficients.\n"),
  band[1], band[2], cov_band[1], cov_band[2]))
```

## Correctness checks

Score vectors, the observed information, and the null-space treatment are
validated mechanically; the bootstrap row compares the delta-method SEs with
a nonparametric bootstrap SD on one MCAR dataset (n = 200).

```{r checks}
checks$value <- signif(checks$value, 3)
knitr::kable(checks, col.names = c("Check", "Statistic", "Value",
                                   "Tolerance", "Pass"))
```

## Calibration

`ratio_*` is mean SE over Monte Carlo SD (1 is perfect); `cover_*` is
Wald-z 95% coverage. Truth is exact (implied kappa of the true parameters)
on `ds5x6_severity`; on `copula5x6_high` the model is misspecified and
coverage is taken around the mechanism-specific pseudo-true value estimated
from one large fit, so those rows inherit a small Monte Carlo blur.

```{r calibration}
disp <- summary[, c("dgp", "mechanism", "n", "weight", "coefficient",
                    "bias", "sd", "ratio_ml", "ratio_robust",
                    "cover_ml", "cover_robust")]
num <- vapply(disp, is.numeric, logical(1))
disp[num] <- lapply(disp[num], function(x) round(x, 3))
knitr::kable(disp, col.names = c("DGP", "Mechanism", "n", "Weight",
                                 "Coefficient", "Bias", "SD", "SE/SD (ML)",
                                 "SE/SD (robust)", "Coverage (ML)",
                                 "Coverage (robust)"))
```

## Caveats

- Coverage error at small n mixes point bias (study 29: DS-FIML retains
  finite-sample bias at n = 40) with SE error; the se/sd ratio isolates the
  SE side.
- The weak spot is anchor-MAR with quadratic weights at n <= 100: se/sd
  drops to about 0.6-0.7 and Wald coverage to 0.67-0.80. The optimism is
  broad, not an outlier artifact (se over an IQR-based sd is still ~0.70 at
  n = 100), and `null_frac` does not reliably flag the failing replicates
  there. This is the same regime where study 29 already prefers nt_fiml on
  quadratic MAR; at n = 400 the MAR cells calibrate fine (se/sd 0.91-0.93,
  coverage 0.92-0.93).
- The pseudo-true values for the misspecified cells come from one fit at
  n = 300{,}000, so their coverage entries carry roughly +/- 0.002 truth
  error, noticeable against an n = 400 sampling SD of about 0.02.
- The probe validates the experiment-local R implementation only; nothing
  here gates the C++ core.

## Reproduce

```{r repro, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf("Seed base %s, %s replications per cell, run %s.\n\n",
            meta$seed_base, meta$reps, meta$timestamp))
```

```sh
Rscript run_experiment.R --checks --calibrate --reps 500
```
